Here's what I got from exercising Entire live against this repo — plus the one piece of "simulated action" that needs your go-ahead.

## What Entire is already doing (no action needed)

It's silently recording **this very session** as I work. `entire session current` shows:

```
Session 9f40ebd0…  ·  Claude Code  ·  claude-opus-4-8[1m]  ·  active
Turns: 2   Tokens: 109.5k (Input 4 · Cache read 77.5k · Cache write 31.2k · Output 779)
Last prompt: "this repo uses the new entire.io link. i want to see some simulated action…"
```

And `entire session tokens` even gives optimization advice:
> *Cache write is elevated; avoid broad new context and narrow the next read before continuing.*

So the baseline benefit: **every agent session (prompts, model, turns, token economics) is captured automatically** — no setup per session.

## The payoff features — and why they're empty right now

| Command | What it gives you | Status in this repo |
|---|---|---|
| `entire why <file>:<line>` | The commit **+ checkpoint + the AI prompt + session** that produced a line | Needs ≥1 committed checkpoint |
| `entire search "..."` | Semantic search across checkpoints/commits/sessions | `no matching repositories… is the repo mirrored?` |
| `entire checkpoint list` | Agent work bundled per commit | `checkpoints 0` |
| `entire recap` / `activity` | Throughput / iteration / continuity / streak, you vs team | `0 sessions` |

They're all empty for one reason: **agent work only becomes a checkpoint when you commit it**, and nothing's been committed through Entire yet. This repo is brand-new to it.

## The simulated action to actually *see* it

To demonstrate the whole loop end-to-end, I'd:
1. Create a throwaway file (e.g. `scratch/entire-demo.md`) on a short-lived branch `entire-demo`
2. Commit it → watch it become a **checkpoint** linked to this session
3. Run `entire why scratch/entire-demo.md:1` → show it tracing the line back to *this prompt*
4. Run `entire checkpoint list` / `search` → now populated
5. Delete the branch to leave `master` untouched

That commit is the only write involved (everything else was read-only). Your CLAUDE.md says commit only when asked, and the Entire hook says ask before writes — so I want your OK first.

========== MIRROR ADD HELP ==========
entire repo mirror add — Mirror a repository onto one or more clusters
With no arguments, launches an interactive wizard: pick repos to mirror, pick one or more regions, then creates every (repo, region) mirror in parallel and prints the clone URLs. --cluster requires a <repo>.

With a <repo>, places it on every cluster named by --cluster — repeat the flag or comma-separate the hosts — in parallel, then waits for each to become usable. Pass --no-wait to return as soon as the placements are registered. Idempotent on (repo, cluster), so naming a cluster the repo is already on reports it rather than failing.

When --cluster is omitted, an interactive terminal offers the available clusters as a multi-select; non-interactive runs default to aws-us-east-2.entire.io.

With an /et/ ref, places replicas of an Entire-native repo and waits for each to be seeded. A native mirror goes in a region other than the repo's own, so only those clusters are offered and --cluster has no default there: non-interactive runs must name one.

Every cluster is attempted: one that fails does not stop the others, and the command exits non-zero naming the ones that did.

Repository references name their forge: /gh/<owner>/<repo> for a GitHub mirror, /et/<project>/<repo> for an Entire-native repository.

Examples:
entire repo mirror add

input.command:
cd /Users/kumagopa/code/home/home
git checkout -b entire-review-demo 2>&1
mkdir -p scripts/backups
cat > scripts/backups/prune-old-backups.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Prune Proxmox backup dumps older than the retention window.
# Intended to run from cron on a Proxmox host.
set -u

RETENTION_DAYS=7
BACKUP_DIR="${BACKUP_DIR}"

echo "Pruning backups older than $RETENTION_DAYS days in $BACKUP_DIR"

# BUG 1: if BACKUP_DIR is empty/unset this expands to "rm -rf /*" style disaster
rm -rf $BACKUP_DIR/*.tmp

# BUG 2: -mtime comparison wrong operator; this deletes files NEWER than retention
find $BACKUP_DIR -name "*.vma.zst" -mtime -$RETENTION_DAYS -exec rm {} \;

# BUG 3: exit status of the loop not checked; always reports success
for f in $(ls $BACKUP_DIR); do
  echo "kept: $f"
done

echo "Prune complete"
exit 0
EOF
git add scripts/backups/prune-old-backups.sh
